assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a general, predictable, ligand-controlled operation. It is among the most used reactions in medicinal chemistry and process synthesis, and it fits the synthetic-efficiency criterion of fewer steps and broad scope.
assessment.attribution: Kosugi's tin-amide precedent was an early proof of concept; the practical, general catalytic amination with amines and later ligand generations is the decisive work of Buchwald and Hartwig, who developed it independently and in parallel. A two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent confirmation and industrial use; the field is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be argued to have covered the area.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees C-N coupling as a distinct discovery or an extension of the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Relative weight of Kosugi's early stoichiometric precedent is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional handles; directing-group and ligand-controlled Pd chemistry delivers site selectivity that shortens routes to complex molecules.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many groups (Yu, Sanford, Hartwig, Daugulis, Smith). Yu's ligand-enabled and remote-selective methods and Sanford's Pd(II/IV) and mechanism work are the most distinctive. Overlap with Hartwig's borylation and amination work complicates a trio.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted in discovery and some late-stage industrial work, but selectivity and generality for truly unbiased substrates remain partly unsolved, and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit and priority disputes across directing-group, borylation and Pd(II/IV) strands.
Some of the field may be considered too young or too incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new, mild radical manifold for synthesis with broad application in pharmaceutical chemistry and has changed how bond constructions are designed.
assessment.attribution: Stephenson, Yoon and MacMillan reported the founding 2008-2009 reports; MacMillan is already a laureate (2021) so I propose others, with Nicewicz for organic photocatalysts. Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre complicate a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent reproduction and industrial uptake within about 15 years. Timing is reasonable though the mechanistic literature is still maturing.
uncertainties: Priority vs. earlier photochemistry and the MacMillan overlap with a prior prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides and made total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine, with a conceptual elegance that I as a synthetic chemist value.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed native chemical ligation; Muir expanded it to expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are later contributors with major but secondary roles.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and used for protein engineering and therapeutic proteins for about 30 years.
uncertainties: Whether expressed protein ligation is a distinct discovery from NCL.
Competing claims from Danishefsky and Liu.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of KRAS G12C via the switch-II pocket overturned the view that KRAS was undruggable, and his earlier analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics added a general tool. Major translational impact through approved drugs.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is concentrated in a single person. Drug development by industry builds on the Shokat concept.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated by approved inhibitors but only within a few years of the first approvals; durable resistance questions remain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes demonstrated that these species can be bottled, and N-heterocyclic and cyclic alkyl amino carbenes became ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, underpinning modern catalysis including Ru metathesis catalysts.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's earlier stable phosphinocarbene work and Arduengo's NHC are the key isolations; Nolan, Rovis and Bode are major application developers but not the originators.
assessment.maturity: Mature, since 1991, with large independent impact. Part of the effect has already been seen in the metathesis prize.
uncertainties: Choice of originators vs. application developers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs established metal-free activation of H2 and small molecules and opened a conceptually distinct reactivity paradigm in main-group catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 H2 activation is the key discovery and Erker contributed major work on the reactivity and scope; two-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Mature conceptually, but practical catalytic impact is still modest relative to transition metal catalysis.
uncertainties: Practical utility compared to the importance of concept.
Earlier related observations from other groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues creates a new modality in which chemistry hijacks ubiquitin ligases, with large therapeutic prospects.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies defined the PROTAC concept; Ciulli developed VHL ligands and structure-guided design. Handa, Ito and others link thalidomide to cereblon, so credit is contested between the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands.
assessment.maturity: Clinical programs are in progress with no definitive approval for PROTACs, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Contested allocation between PROTAC and cereblon glue lines.
